newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH HANDLOWY GIVES VISTULA LIMIT RATE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH HANDLOWY GIVES VISTULA LIMIT RATE.

text.p: The Polish Bank Handlowy SA brokerage rated the garment maker Vistula SA as limit, pointing out its good position in the sector but stressing low demand for its products, Handlowy said in a report dated September 6.
"After summing up all advantages and disadvantages of the company we believe it is worth keeping in portfolio, but in a shorter position," the report said.

It said that among the company's advantages were a broad assortment offer, a 3.5-4 percent market share, good financial results in comparison to other garment makers and possible rise in exports to countries of the former Soviet Union.
But it stressed relatively low demand for men's clothing in Poland and declining profitability of processing exports.
It said Vistula's net profit was likely to rise to 9.8 million zlotys in 1996 and to 11 million zlotys next year, up from last year's 8.4 million.
It said it expected the firm's sales to rise to 103 million zlotys in 1996 and 124 million in 1997, up from last year's 87 million zlotys.
